shape: a parent's odd habit that the child only understands years later

slides.text: my mum packed two yellow apples in my navy school bag every single morning, even though i never ate them.
so every afternoon i brought them home bruised, and she put them in the bin without a word.
but she kept putting two in the front pocket, right next to my pencil case.
so yesterday while we were clearing out the old pantry, i asked her why she wasted all those apples.
she folded the brown paper bag and said [[you never brought lunch]] on tuesdays.
so she made sure there was extra in my bag, so i could hand one over without making a fuss.
[[she never said your name]], but for five years she fed the quiet kid who sat next to me in row three.

caption:
my mum still asks about you every time i call her on sunday.
she never forgot the year we shared a desk in the back corner.
send this to the best friend who shared your desk in school.
